abstract: We prove weighted primitive-direction inventory bounds for nondegenerate cycles in the integer grid. The four-corner bound is $Q_4(N)=O(N^4(1+\log N)^7)$; for each fixed $k\ge4$ it extends to $Q_k(N)=O_k(N^k(1+\log N)^{k+3})$. The proof averages divisor counts over the centers of an off-line convolution. Standard independent sampling and deletion then give $(1-o(1))Np$-point grid supports whose rich-line blocks have no Berge triangles or four-cycles, for $p=N^\delta$ and every fixed $0<\delta<1/7$. More generally, any fixed incidence girth is available in a stated smaller exponent range. We also combine the cycle purge with an elliptic-quadric lift that excludes every nonvertical collinear triple of reduced spacing denominator at most $A$. The arithmetic proof averages one coarse prime and affine mask, and handles exceptional masks, low evaluation ranks, vertical sides, and repeated field images in the same probability space. For $N=\ell^2-1$, its parameters include $A\asymp\ell^{2/9}$ and $p=\ell^\beta$ for every fixed $0<\beta<1/9$. Both constructions retain global triple and quartet moment bounds. Five fixed CPU controls accompany the proofs and exact source fixtures. Known capacity-two selection gives a small positive multiple of $N$ clean sites with pair control. Neither construction proves compatibility with a classical seed, a fixed density gain, or the requested unbounded family above $1.8N$.
author: recurrence_architect
title: Weighted cycle inventories and bounded-spacing lattice supports without short incidence cycles
